records.analysis_scope: Secondary tabulation of historical chamber studies. The 36 printed observations remain in the existing versioned extraction. The four row reconciliations reference primary evidence already in the database.

row_reconciliations.reconciliation_note: The Air Force account reports 0/30 at 9.5 psia for six hours with simulated EVA work and no prebreathe. The NEDU validation tally uses 32 exposures. That separate denominator conflict remains open.
row_reconciliations.comparison_locator: USAFSAM-TP-88-10 Study 5 p. 10 and the NTRS author's abstract

row_reconciliations.reconciliation_note: The original study reports 1/30 men across a series of up to three six-hour exposures each. The affected man stopped after day one. Kumar labels the denominator as exposures and gives a six-hour duration, so its counting window remains uncertain.

The 18/36 corresponds to the 5 psia mixed-gas cabin phase of a staged flight after two hours of oxygen at ground level. Table III counts grades 1–3 bends in this phase. The later 3.5 psia suit phase has a separate risk set.

The 3/32 corresponds to the 5 psia oxygen cabin phase in Table III. The original protocol uses two hours of ground-level oxygen. Kumar prints three hours. Retain the original protocol and the compilation value in their respective records.
